content:
jamie: heads up — saw 95th/99th tail latency spikes during eviction floods on tiny tenants. digging into prefix cache metrics, looks correlated with bursty demotes + immediate hard-evict churn.

anika: ugh. can you paste the grafana panel?

jamie: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-prefix/evict-rate?orgId=1 (spike at ~09:14 UTC)

ops-bot: alert: evict_rate > 200/s on node-rw-12 for 4m :warning:

liam: my suspicion: our fast-path demote -> immediate eviction leaves in-flight requests with stale residency flags, forcing reads to backend. that amplifies latency.

david: agreed. two levers: (a) introduce a soft-evict state + hysteresis window, or (b) prefer demote-to-cached-stub where we keep small KV meta for short period.

anika: prefer (a) first since it's lower-risk. soft-evict means we mark prefix as "evict_pending" and only complete eviction after N seconds or when memory pressure demands.

jamie: proposal sketch:
```
# prefix cache hysteresis config (proposal)
evict_hysteresis_ms: 5000        # wait before full eviction
evict_soft_state_ttl_ms: 15000  # keep lightweight meta after soft-evict
evict_priority_decay: 0.6       # decay hotness score when demoted
```

liam: that matches my thinking. two questions: 1) what should the soft-state contain (just header + last-access-ts?), 2) how do we surface fallback behavior so reads don't hit backend heavy?

anika: soft-state = header + minimal KV pointer + cached small-K bytes for top-k tokens (cheap). on read path: if state == evict_pending, serve from small-K cache or async-prefetch and return a 202-ish placeholder to caller (we already have structured fallbacks).

david: placeholder responses are risky for host APIs. better: synchronous async-prefetch if request latency budget allows, otherwise fall back to a cheaper model variant. we need per-tenant QoS toggles.

jamie: implementation detail: maintain two eviction queues: normal and forced. hysteresis only applies to normal. forced evict (e.g., OOM) bypasses hysteresis. also add a metric: evict_hysteresis_skipped_count.

liam: can we avoid global locks? design sketch: per-shard atomic CAS on prefix state (HOT -> DEMOTED -> EVICT_PENDING -> EVICTED). transitions idempotent.\
small pseudo: 
```
if CAS(state==DEMOTED, state=EVICT_PENDING): schedule timer(hysteresis_ms)
on timer: if last_access < demote_time + hysteresis_ms: CAS(EVICT_PENDING -> EVICTED)
```

david: sounds good. watch for timer explosion — better to batch timers per shard and sweep.

anika: +1 to sweep. also add telemetry: time_in_evict_pending, rehydrate_count, prefetch_succeeded_percent.

jamie: tradeoffs: increases memory footprint for soft-state and complexity in counters. upside: reduces read amplification and tail spikes.

sre-alex: ops concern: if hysteresis is too long, cold memory pressure might cause us to OOM before forced eviction; need graceful backstop config. propose default hysteresis 5s and max_soft_state_bytes_per_shard = 64MB.

liam: ok. plan: jamie will open a follow-up RFC PR with config, metrics, and CAS state machine. i'll prototype per-shard sweep timer and small-K cache. anika/david will review safety and fallback UX.

jamie: I'll also add a canary run plan: enable on staging pool 3, ramp to 10% of traffic, watch 95/99 latency + evict_hysteresis_skipped_count.

anika: assign liam to the prototype, jamie to RFC. david to own canary watch. sre-alex to set alerts for OOM and evict_rate.

liam: noted. starting spike prototype tomorrow. :coffee:

jamie: thanks all — filing the RFC now.
